{{Top}}
{{Quote|Oddball, do you copy?''"<br />"''Copy, Red Leader.''"<br />"''Mark my position and form your squad behind me.|[[Jedi General/Legends|Jedi General]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to [[Clone Commander/Legends|clone trooper commander]] [[Davijaan/Legends|Davijaan]] during the [[Battle of Coruscant/Legends|Battle of Coruscant]]|<ref name="Episode 3">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
[[File:StormtroopersDS1.jpg|thumb|right|250px|A squad of Stormtroopers aboard the first Death Star.]]
A '''squad''' was the smallest military unit in many of the galaxy's army formations. The numbers of [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] in a squad varied, but usually consisted of no more than a dozen personnel.

==The Clone Wars==
===Republic army===
Under the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], squads of ten or twelve soldiers were common among the army forces,<ref name="ISB2">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref> but in the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] created during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], a standard [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone trooper]] squad consisted of nine soldiers, led by a commanding [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeant]], with four squads forming a [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]].<ref name="TCWCG">''[[The Clone Wars Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Although the GAR squads, and later [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] squads, were smaller in amount than the Old Republic squads, they made up for the comparative lack of manpower by utilizing superior training as well as a more thorough usage of coordinated small-unit tactics.<ref name="ISB2" />

Otherwise, [[Special forces/Legends|elite]] clone of the [[Special Operations Brigade/Legends|Special Operations Brigade]], including [[Clone commando/Legends|clone commandos]], [[clone assassin]]s and [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC commandos]] operated in squads of four,<ref name="TCWCG" /> such as [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]].<ref name="RC">''[[Star Wars: Republic Commando]]''</ref> The four men squad included a sergeant and five such squads formed a [[Troop/Legends|troop]].<ref name="TCWCG" />

[[Republic Peace Officer]] squads were made of five men.<ref name="Star Wars 1998 28">[[Star Wars (1998) 28|''Star Wars'' (1998) 28]]</ref>

===CIS army===
In the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]], the [[Order of Battle/Legends|Order of Battle]] of its different members was maintained. [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] infantry squads were made of eight [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droids]], without squad leader, with seven squads forming a platoon. [[Warrior caste (Geonosian)/Legends|Geonosian warriors]] did not have any military organization. [[Commerce Guild/Legends|Commerce Guild]] infantry squads were made of six [[Gossam/Legends|Gossam]] soldiers, including a squad leader, with six squads forming a troop. [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] infantry squads were made of twelve [[Koorivar Fusiliers/Legends|Koorivar Fusiliers]], led by a sergeant, with three squads forming a platoon. [[InterGalactic Banking Clan/Legends|IGBC]] infantry squads were made of nine [[Muun/Legends|Muun]] Guards or nine battle droids, led by a sergeant, with five squads forming a troop.<ref name="TCWCG" />

==Galactic Empire==
===Imperial Army===
When the Republic gave way to the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], the non-clone line forces of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] retained the GAR's standard squad strength of a sergeant and eight other [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|troopers]]. On the sergeant's recommendation, one soldier was normally appointed [[Corporal/Legends|Corporal]], also known as the "one-man", and a brevet list was created which numbered each trooper down to the "eight-man", denoting the order in which authority devolved to them if the squad's more senior soldiers were killed. This likewise led to the expressions "Lower than the eight-man" and "Certain as the one-man's mind."<ref name="ISB2" />

As with larger units Imperial Army squads could be [[Imperial Army/Legends#Agumentation|augmented]], with two squads paired together. In these instances the sergeant of the first squad was given the brevit rank of "lead sergeant" and his corporal directed their squad during his absence. More commonly a squad was just augmented with a small detachment, typically a heavy weapons detail supporting a line squad.<ref name="ISB2" />

By the time of the aftermath of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], the Empire had been experimenting with the usage of smaller squads, although these were still rare, with the 8-man squad still acting as the backbone of the Imperial Army.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Line Squad====
{{Main|Line squad}}
[[File:Line_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
Infantry units were called "line" units in the Army, and the line squad was considered the backbone of the army. However, high losses against the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] caused the Empire to rethink how they could improve the line squad as cost-effectively as possible. This led to the process of equipping each squad with a [[Light repeating blaster/Legends|Light repeating blaster]] to increase their short range firepower. However, only in three [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] were more than half of the squads equipped with these blasters by the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]: the [[Shwuy sector/Legends|Shwuy sector]], [[Harron sector/Legends|Harron]] and [[Nembus sector/Legends|Nembus sector]]. On heavily populated worlds such as [[Uviuy Exen/Legends|Uviuy Exen]] and [[Trammen]], every line squad was equipped with a light repeating blaster.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Heavy Weapons Squad====
{{Main|Heavy weapons squad}}
[[File:Heavy_weapons_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
These [[heavy weapon]] squads were armed with either two- to three-man [[Medium repeating blaster/Legends|Medium repeating blasters]] or three-man [[Heavy repeating blaster/Legends|Heavy repeating blasters]]. Heavy weapons squads were usually attached to other platoons in order to provide additional firepower.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Sharpshooter Squad====
{{Main|Sharpshooter squad}}
[[File:Sharpshooter_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
These squads consisted of [[Imperial Army Special Missions trooper/Legends|Special Missions troopers]] who had shown accuracy above standard with their weapons and could "reach out and touch" the enemy at a distance. Each trooper also received basic demolition and other training, and while not officially part of their Order of Battle practically every squad included a light repeating blaster. Due to their above average skill sets and training, the brevet corporal would be chosen prior to deployment based on the type of mission the squad was assigned, while each trooper was expected to improvise on the battlefield should both NCOs be incapacitated.<ref name="ISB2" /><ref name="SpecForce">''[[Rules of Engagement: The Rebel SpecForce Handbook]]''</ref>

====Engineering Squad====
{{Main|Engineering squad}}
[[File:Engineering_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
Engineering Squads were composed of [[Imperial Army Special Missions trooper/Legends|Special Missions troopers]] trained in a variety of combat engineering skills. Engineering squads were expected to get into, get around or go over any obstacle through the creative use of explosives. As the only Imperial tech-squad directly involved in combat they were also expected to be able to operate, repair and dismantle nearly any equipment and gear found on a mission. One of the squad's members would also be a demolition expert with experience operating as part of the sharpshooter squad, making them doubly dangerous. These squads had no standard gear, and would use anything they could get their hands on, such as [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]], [[Medpac/Legends|medpacs]] or Portable Sensor Arrays.<ref name="ISB2" /><ref name="SpecForce" />

====Repulsorlift Squad====
{{Main|Repulsorlift squad}}
[[File:Repulsorlift_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
These mechanized squads had the same composition as line squads with the addition of two light repulsorlift transports. Each vehicle had a crew of four, consisting of a mechanic, a driver, a sensor/tech officer and a gunner/commander. The sergeant's vehicle was equipped with an additional [[Dedicated energy receptor/Legends|DER]] and operator located in the transport compartment.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Heavy Weapons Repulsorlift Squad====
{{Main|Heavy weapons repulsorlift squad}}
[[File:Heavy_weapons_repulsorlift_squad.jpg|right|150px]]
Heavy Weapons Repulsorlift Squads had additional armaments built into their vehicles, such as a heavy repeating blaster, a [[4.4 grenade launcher]] or [[Laser cannon/Legends|light laser cannon]]. These weapons could be dismounted and used by the infantry for additional firepower.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Scout Squad (Lance)====
{{Main|Scout lance}}
[[File:Scout_lance.jpg|right|150px]]
A scout squad was also called a scout "lance". Consisting of five personnel including the sergeant, they were generally equipped with [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bikes]] with a few also using two-man vehicles. Scout troopers were trained to repair and maintain their bikes, which reduced the need for support personnel. In contrast to the more usual practice, the Empire emphasized unit heritage and pride in its scout squads, which were often recruited from worlds with a strong tradition of mounted warriors.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Armor Section====
{{Main|Armor section}}
[[File:Armor_section.jpg|right|150px]]
An armor section consisted of either two light or medium repulsortank (or their equivalent) or a single heavy repulsortank (or it's equivalent). These units existed only as part of the Order of Battle for an armor platoon and never deployed by themselves.<ref name="ISB2" />

====Artillery Section====
{{Main|Artillery section}}
[[File:Artillery_section.jpg|right|150px]]
Similar to an armor section the artillery section consisted of either two light artillery pieces or one medium or heavy artillery piece. However an artillery section could be deployed by itself to support another platoon, a process known as "grafting," although this only took place if there was enough time before an attack to plan.<ref name="ISB2" />

===Stormtroopers and scout troopers===
Just as the standard Army squad consisted of eight soldiers and a sergeant, Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|Stormtrooper]] squads were said to have nine men as standard in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]; a nine-man squad would also fit with an implied stormtrooper [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] strength of 45 men, and the ten-man stormtrooper bodyguard assigned to a [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] was perhaps a nine-man squad plus an officer in command. However, Rebel sources believed that the Empire was also using smaller stormtrooper squads, and by [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]], the standard squad of the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] apparently consisted of units of four troopers, such as [[Unit Aurek-Seven]], one of ten such units in [[Aurek Company]]. According to Section 682.T.ST88 of the ''Imperial Stormtrooper Corps Field Manual'', although the minimum unit allowed in the Stormtrooper Corps was a squad, the squad itself could be subdivided further into two fire teams and organized into wedge formations, with the fire team leader being at the tip of each wedge, in order to permit maximum firing range in every direction and allow ready communication between members, which was usually advised when the composition or position of enemy forces were uncertain.<ref name="IHB">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>

By [[137 ABY]], a squad in the [[407th Stormtrooper Division]] consisted of four troopers led by a sergeant. One of the troopers was armed with a heavy support weapon, while the others used conventional blaster rifles. Their officer was a lieutenant, but so far the number of squads in a platoon or company is unknown.

Imperial [[Scout trooper/Legends|scout troopers]] were organized differently, drawing both recruits and traditions from worlds where cavalry combat had a prominent history. They were organized in five-man units known as [[Scout lance|lances]], with each trooper being expected to care for his own mount&mdash;usually a one-seater speeder bike like the [[74-Z speeder bike/Legends|Aratech 74-Z]], although some lances combined one bike with a pair of two-seat flyers. Additionally, although part of the [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]], scout troopers were often integrated into the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]] order-of-battle: two lances, together known as a [[scout squadron]], were combined with two infantry squads in each [[Platoon/Legends|platoon]] of a [[Battalion/Legends|Repulsorlift Battalion's]] [[Company/Legends|scout troop]], while the [[Platoon/Legends|scout platoon]] of a [[Company/Legends|special missions company]] consisted entirely of biker scouts.

==Other military forces==
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], squads comparable to those of Imperial forces served as the most basic component elements of [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[Alliance Special Forces/Legends|SpecForces]] regiments, but for active duty, mission-specific units were formed with little regard for the nominal roster or formal organizational doctrine.

In the [[Chiss Expansionary Defense Force]], a standard squad apparently numbered six warriors, divided into two half-squads of three.<ref name="Survivor's Quest">''[[Survivor's Quest]]''</ref>

Among the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]], squads (such as [[Viper Alpha]], [[Vertigo Company|Vertigo]], and [[Headhunter Company|Headhunter]]) were larger than in other armed forces; this may be due to the fact that the Mandalorians seemed to use "squad" and "[[Company/Legends|company]]" interchangeably.

For [[Warrior caste|Yuuzhan Vong warriors]], three squads composed a [[Triad (unit)/Legends|unit]].
